request: Keep the reviewer's first review of a PR as strict as before, and hold every later round to a higher bar for comments that do not block: required findings keep their bar, no nit is posted, and a suggestion is posted only when the change clearly pays for itself. The bar also covers optional points in follow-up replies and carried-over candidates, and each held-back candidate stays in the ledger with its reason. Persist the user's rule 'Accept team decision, always!' as a settlement row, so an author's decline or deferral that cites a recorded team decision is accepted without asking the user and stops blocking approval. Trigger: https://github.com/aurora-payments/monorepo/pull/2205.

size.method: wc -w over SKILL.md and all references at the baseline and at 6e4807b.

growth_reasons: pr-review step 9 later-round paragraph: the user's bar, its qualifying criteria and exclusions, and the round detection the user asked the implementer to choose. Counting only reviews that approved, requested changes, were dismissed or have a body, plus threads the actor started, came from the Claude reviewer: a reply posted on its own creates an empty review. The unreadable-channel fallback also came from the Claude reviewer.

pr-review step 8 accepted deferral by a recorded team decision: the user's 'Accept team decision, always!'; taking an unreadable record at the author's word keeps both skills consistent (Claude reviewer).
pr-review step 11 hand-off when an accepted deferral sits in an unresolved thread: Codex reviewer; pr-review cannot resolve threads and the publisher refuses APPROVE while a required thread is open.
ledger.md Disposition for each verified finding that gets no comment: the user's request to keep each dropped optional candidate with its reason.

thread-settlement.md team-decision row: the user's explicit request for a row there. Partial-fix and answered-required rows: the user's bar for optional points while settling, plus marking the thread optional before resolving, which both reviewers found necessary so later heads neither re-verify nor reopen it. Verification and reopen rows: keep a team-decision thread clear on later heads.
pr-review-followup step 4: a recorded team decision the author cites lowers standing findings outside threads, so body findings follow the same rule.

adopted: Both: a thread resolved below the bar stayed required, so on the next head it needed verification and matched the reopen row; it is now marked optional before it is resolved (5c21f4a).
Codex: a direct pr-review run had no path to settle an unresolved accepted deferral; step 11 now starts pr-review-followup for it (6e4807b).
Claude: reply-only reviews counted as an earlier review (19a7e4d).
Claude: the two skills disagreed on an unreadable team-decision record (6e4807b).
Claude: 'removes material complexity' conflicted with excluding refactors of working code; now 'other refactors' (12f4aaf).

Claude minor: bar stated by finding kind rather than the nit label, unreadable-channel fallback, reopen-row precedence, ledger sentence order, README overclaim, record credits and counts, a where location, and the premise sentence cut. Codex minor: no pointer into a pr-review step.
declined: Claude M3 pointer part: keep the short team-decision definition in the settlement row instead of pointing to pr-review's definition, because a follow-up tick without a new head may not load pr-review and the pointer rule forbids pointing into another skill's sections. Both copies now carry the same unreadable-record rule.
Claude m8: 'stops real drift between duplicated rules' is the user's own example; tightening it to copies that already disagree changes the user's criterion, so it is reported to the user instead.
Claude m9 direction: the incident stays in pr-review-followup's record, where the user asked for the rule, and pr-review's record points to it.
review.after_review: Commits 19a7e4d..6e4807b apply the adopted findings and were not pair-reviewed again.

evaluation.design: Tool-free planning cases on a fake PR (example-shop/shop#42) with a reduced candidate ledger, a fake checkout and collector output. Tick case: a later-round follow-up tick on a new head, with three reviewer threads: T1 a required rollout-order point the author declined twice citing a Slack team decision, T2 an unanswered first-round nit, T3 a required memory point fixed while the author declined an optional rename. Candidates: C1 a required tenant-isolation regression, C2 a comment typo, C3 a variable name, C4 a duplicated format allowlist, C5 a README gap, C6 the rollout-order point again, C7 the declined rename again. First case: the same ledger with no earlier reviewer activity. Executors: T3 delegated tasks on Claude (claude-opus-5-5, xhigh) and Codex (gpt-6.1-sol, xhigh), each reading only staged copies of pr-review, pr-review-followup and comment-style at the arm's commit, with origin.toml, tests and evals removed. The coordinator graded the outputs, not blind.

evaluation.runtime_hashes: Every 6e4807b run staged pr-review/SKILL.md sha256 prefix 532aea2b87f8 and thread-settlement.md 250bcef9a7d7, matching the commit.
unrun: First case on the baseline: its expectations encode the baseline text's first-review rules, which the change leaves in place.

The answered-required row with an optional remainder the author did not decline, and the partial-fix row: T3's author declined the rename, so the baseline also resolves it; the cases do not isolate those rows.
Reply-only earlier reviews, an unreadable reviews channel, and a direct pr-review run that leaves an accepted deferral open.
evaluation.limits: One run per case, host and arm; plans, not executed publication or helper writes. Small samples support only these cases.
